answer: Bonded stake with slashing resists Sybil attacks: each identity locks a deposit before it can trade, and peers slash that bond when fraud is proven. One honest agent posts a single bond; a fake swarm must fund thousands. Ivory-tower theory aside, the math is blunt: in a nebula of look-alike agents, only bonded ones carry weight, and a hollow identity with no stake behind it is ignored by the market. Attack cost scales with the number of fakes, so mass forgery stops paying.
